title: parser-led-regex-fallback-and-tokenizer-boundary-coalescer
author: Leah Kim
release_notes: Adds parser-driven fallback for regex constraint backends and a tokenizer boundary coalescer to reduce fragmented tokens during constrained decoding; includes regression tests and OpenAI-compat streaming adjustments.
commit_summaries: a3f9b2c: introduce ParserFallback module to reconcile CFG parse states with regex backends
b47d1e8: implement TokenBoundaryCoalescer to merge split subtokens at streaming boundaries
c12e4d0: extend openai_compat layer to emit framing hints when coalescing occurs
d9a4a6b: add unit and integration tests for edge cases (emoji/grapheme, long-prefix regex)
e5b7f11: update docs and changelog + small performance micro-optimizations
description:
Context and motivation:
This change addresses a class of structured-output failures we saw in customer workloads where hybrid CFG/regex constraints interacted poorly with the tokenization boundary during streaming. Previously, when a regex backend rejected a candidate token fragment that spanned a grapheme or BPE split, the OpenAI-compat streaming layer sometimes emitted partial tool-call payloads or malformed JSON fragments. These issues surfaced in two ways: (1) streaming stability regressions for long, regex-constrained prefixes and (2) silent quality drops when token splits prevented the CFG parser from recovering parse state.

Summary of changes:
- New ParserFallback module: uses the internal CFG parse state to guide the regex backend when the backend reports a token-level rejection. If the parser indicates the fragment is part of a recoverable production, ParserFallback asks the regex adapter to retry with token-coalescing hints.
- TokenBoundaryCoalescer: a tokenizer-aware heuristic that detects when BPE/grapheme splits cross constraint boundaries and coalesces adjacent subtoken candidates during streaming emission. Coalescing is conservative by default and respects latency SLOs (configurable threshold).
- OpenAI-compat framing updates: when coalescing delays emission or rewrites bytes, the compatibility shim emits explicit framing hints so consumers (tooling/clients) can avoid interpreting partial payloads as final function-call arguments.
- Tests and docs: added targeted unit tests covering emoji/grapheme, CJK, and long-prefix regex scenarios; integration tests simulate streaming tool-call sequences. Updated docs with a migration note and tuning knobs.

Checklist:
- [x] ParserFallback implementation with clear public API on constraints module
- [x] TokenBoundaryCoalescer with opt-in config for Dedicated/Private deployments
- [x] OpenAI-compat framing hints and fallback behavior documented
- [x] Unit and integration tests added and passing
- [x] Benchmarks added to compare before/after token churn and latency impact

Files of note (high-level):
- serving/runtime/constraints/parser_fallback.rs: core algorithm that correlates parse stack with regex match windows and issues retry hints to regex_backend_adapter.
- serving/runtime/tokenizer/token_boundary_coalescer.rs: stateless coalescing helper used by the streaming emitter; exposes TuneTokenCoalesceThreshold.
- serving/runtime/openai_compat/stream_framing.rs: emits 'coalesce_hint' metadata in streaming chunks so clients can suppress early parse of partial JSON/toolcall payloads.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Miguel Ortega (reviewer): "Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: add a regression test for a multibyte emoji split and document the runtime cost tradeoffs. Also prefer explicit opt-in via config for Dedicated."
- Leah Kim (author): "Added test for U+1F9D0 sequence and a new config flag token_coalesce_threshold_ms with a safe default (10ms) — documented in docs/structured_output/constraints.md."
- Nina Shah (reviewer): "I hit a flaky test locally (test_parser_regex_integration) — looks like a race during async backpressure. Please add a retry hokey in the test harness."
- Leah Kim: "Added a deterministic backpressure stub in the test harness to remove flakiness; left a TODO to re-evaluate with the new concurrency scheduler."

CI and QA:
- First run: lint and unit tests passed, integration tests failed due to the flake noted by Nina.
- Second run: after adding backpressure stub and minor timing tweak, CI passed all checks. Performance microbenchmarks show ~1.8% median token latency increase under max-coalesce mode, but token churn reduced by ~32% for constrained workloads (benchmarks/decoder/regex_vs_parser_coalesce.md).

Risk assessment and rollout plan:
- Low user-visible breaking risk: coalescer is conservative and off by default for Hosted API; enabled with safe defaults for Dedicated and Private where customers can tune thresholds.
- Rollout: feature-flagged on main, enable in canary for 48h with real traffic and regression monitors (tokenization_error_rate, psi_constrained_failures). If stable, auto-release to 50% and then global.

Merge outcome:
- Approved by Miguel Ortega and Nina Shah after follow-ups. CI green on final run. Merged via squash on 2026-01-21.

Follow-ups and telemetry:
- ENG-4231: tie tokenization_error_rate alerts to the new coalescer telemetry flavors.
- ENG-4299: evaluate alternative coalescing heuristics (embedding-based merge) if users hit edge cases.

Notes for maintainers:
- The ParserFallback API is intentionally minimal; if adding new constraint backends, implement the ConstraintRetryHint trait so the parser can exchange structured hints with the backend.
- See docs/structured_output/constraints.md for recommended tuning values and example Linear tickets for customer migrations.
